name: BS170
title: BS170 / MMBF170: 60 V, 500 mA N-channel enhancement-mode MOSFET in TO-92 and SOT-23
summary: A small-signal N-channel enhancement-mode DMOS transistor rated 60 V drain to source and 500 mA continuous drain current, with an on-resistance of 5 Ω maximum at VGS = 10 V. The same die comes as the through-hole BS170 in TO-92 and the surface-mount MMBF170 in SOT-23; the two differ in pulsed current, power dissipation, thermal resistance and safe operating area. Uses named for it are small servo motor control, driving the gates of larger power MOSFETs, and general low-voltage, low-current switching.

circuits.title: Switching test circuit
circuits.description: Measures the turn-on and turn-off times. A pulse generator drives the gate of the device under test through RGEN; the drain is loaded by RL from the VDD terminal and the source goes to ground. The input is observed at the gate (VIN) and the output at the drain (VOUT). The switching rows use VDD = 25 V and VGS = 10 V, with ID = 200 mA and RGEN = 25 Ω for the BS170, ID = 500 mA and RGEN = 50 Ω for the MMBF170.

operation.text: An N-channel enhancement-mode transistor made in a dense-cell DMOS process to keep on-resistance low. It switches quickly, is rugged and reliable, and serves as a small-signal switch, controlled by its gate voltage, for loads up to 500 mA DC; its saturation current is high.

BS170 (TO-92) and MMBF170 (SOT-23) share every electrical limit and characteristic except pulsed drain current (1200 mA against 800 mA), power dissipation (830 mW against 300 mW, derated by 6.6 or 2.4 mW/°C above 25 °C), junction-to-ambient thermal resistance (150 against 417 °C/W), the transconductance and switching-time test conditions, the safe operating area (Figures 13 and 14) and the transient thermal response (Figures 15 and 16).

VOUT is taken inverted, rising as the drain falls. td(on) runs from the input crossing 10 % to the output crossing 10 %; tr is the output's travel from 10 % to 90 %; ton = td(on) + tr. td(off) runs from the falling input crossing 90 % to the output crossing 90 %; tf is the output's travel from 90 % back to 10 %; toff = td(off) + tf. Pulse width is taken between the input's 50 % points.

Each safe operating area holds for VGS = 10 V, a single pulse and TA = 25 °C. The boundary is set at low voltage by on-resistance, then by a flat current limit (near 1.2 A for the BS170, near 0.8 A for the MMBF170), then by pulse-length lines from 100 µs to DC, and finally by the 60 V drain-source rating.

Tape-and-reel: five reels per 375 mm × 267 mm × 375 mm intermediate box. Ammo: each ammo pack sits in a 327 mm × 158 mm × 135 mm box, five of them per 333 mm × 231 mm × 183 mm intermediate box. Bulk: 2000 units per EO70 box (114 mm × 102 mm × 51 mm) with anti-static bubble sheets, five EO70 boxes per 530 mm × 130 mm × 83 mm intermediate box, 10,000 units at most.

Parts travel in embossed carrier tape of carbon-loaded dissipative polycarbonate under a heat-activated multilayer polyester cover tape. The standard option is 3000 parts on a 7-inch (177 mm) dark-blue anti-static polystyrene reel; option D87Z is 10,000 parts on a 13-inch (330 mm) reel. Labelled reels go into recyclable corrugated boxes, five reels at most per box.

Three pads, each 1.00 mm wide and 1.40 mm long. The two pads on one side sit 1.90 mm apart centre to centre; the single pad on the other side is centred 0.95 mm from either of them across, with the two rows 2.20 mm apart centre to centre.
